reason: I'm not sending my clients' ticket data and contracts to a company I've never heard of, DPA or not. And I already pay for a reconciliation/BI tool that's meant to catch unbilled licences, so £240 a month on top looks like overlap.
objection: Unknown vendor handling client data. If something goes wrong it's my reputation with my clients, and a DPA from a startup doesn't give me much comfort. Beyond that, I think my existing tool already covers most of this.
would_change_my_mind: Several MSP owners I know of on r/msp or in the LinkedIn groups vouching for it, plus Cyber Essentials Plus or ISO 27001. Then I'd try the free audit to see whether it finds anything my current tool misses.
